Definition: from G4920; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious:--prudent. Compare G5429.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus thanks the Father because He has hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to babes, and He says the same again in Luke, rejoicing in spirit. Paul quotes Isaiah that God will destroy the wisdom of the wise and bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent, and yet Luke calls Sergius Paulus, the deputy of Cyprus, a prudent man who desired to hear the word of God. Prudence is praised in one man and set aside in another, and the difference is whether the prudent one will hear.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God hides His truth from the proudly prudent and reveals it to babes, and I hold that true prudence is a listening heart. Sergius Paulus shows me the difference: a prudent man who wants to hear the word will hear it.
